title: Staff and contractor roster and payroll register, January to June 2026
source_system: Payroll service portal; contractor invoices
what_it_shows: 7 employees by role: Founder and Chief Executive Officer, CTO, Senior Software Engineer, Software Engineer, Customer Success Manager, Account Executive, Operations and Finance Manager; all 7 have Florida addresses and 3 work remotely; 1 part-time contract developer in another U.S. state paid by monthly invoice for about 15 hours a week; 1 departure in the period, the former Customer Success Manager, with a last working day in March 2026; payroll runs biweekly through the outside payroll service

title: Productivity suite users, MFA, administrator roles and MSP account tickets
source_system: Productivity suite admin console (SYS-03), exported by the MSP; MSP help desk tickets
what_it_shows: Named accounts for the 7 employees and the contract developer; MFA enforced for all users by authenticator app push; 2 global administrator accounts held by MSP technicians, both with MFA; single sign-on configured for the repository, support desk and CRM; sign-in throttling and lockout on vendor defaults; the former Customer Success Manager's suite account shows as disabled on the last working day in March 2026; MSP tickets show suite accounts created and disabled on the Operations and Finance Manager's email requests

title: Cloud account identity and access key export
source_system: Cloud provider console (SYS-01)
what_it_shows: Per-person console accounts for the CTO, the Senior Software Engineer, the Software Engineer and the contract developer, each with MFA and the provider's full administrator policy attached; no read-only, deploy-only or break-glass roles defined; 1 long-lived access key with the full administrator policy, created in March 2024, used by the CI pipeline, never rotated

title: Repository and CI/CD settings export
source_system: Source repository host organization settings (SYS-02)
what_it_shows: Members sign in through the suite's single sign-on and MFA is required; the main branch requires one approved pull request review and administrators can bypass it; every merge to main deploys to production; the cloud access key is stored as a CI secret; unit and integration tests run on every pull request; no security, cross-tenant or container image scanning step in the pipeline; dependency vulnerability alerts are on and are sent to the CTO's inbox

title: Application authentication, authorization and admin console settings
source_system: VCP application configuration and code in the repository (SYS-02)
what_it_shows: Customer passwords need 8 characters with no breached-password check and are hashed with an adaptive algorithm; customer accounts lock for 15 minutes after 5 failed sign-ins; MFA is optional for customer users, including customer administrators; 3 customers sign in through their own single sign-on; customer roles are administrator, reviewer and viewer; every database query is filtered by tenant ID in application code; documents are served through short-lived signed links and vendor upload links expire; the internal admin console uses its own local accounts with a password-only login page reachable from the internet; view-as-customer is available to the Customer Success Manager and the engineers, opens any tenant with no approval step, and writes no session record

title: Cloud configuration export: storage, database, network, logging and backups
source_system: Cloud provider console (SYS-01)
what_it_shows: One account in one region; web application, API, workers and the internal admin console on a managed container service; managed relational database and workers in private subnets behind one public load balancer; one object storage bucket of about 165,000 files; storage encryption at rest with provider-managed keys on the database, snapshots and bucket; load balancer TLS policy 1.2 or higher with strict transport security and TLS to the database; database point-in-time recovery 7 days and daily snapshots kept 7 days, both in the production account; bucket versioning off; management event logging at the provider default of 90 days; object-level access logging, database audit logging and the provider's threat detection service available and off; no alert rules configured in the account; application secrets, including the database password and the email delivery and model provider API keys, set as container environment variables; the account's 90-day event history shows no restore jobs

title: Infrastructure code compared with the cloud resource listing
source_system: Repository (SYS-02); cloud provider resource listing (SYS-01)
what_it_shows: About 60% of production resources are defined in infrastructure code; the document bucket policy, some network rules and the database parameter settings were created by hand in the console

title: Production data volumes and tenant settings
source_system: VCP production database (SYS-01), read-only queries run by the CTO
what_it_shows: 47 tenants: 45 active customers and 2 marked terminated, whose contracts ended about 5 and 11 months earlier and whose vendor records and documents are still stored; about 900 active customer users; about 41,000 vendor records with about 52,000 vendor contacts; about 165,000 stored documents; about 29,000 W-9s, of which about 9,800 show a Social Security number as the TIN; about 4,100 of those individuals have Florida addresses and the rest live in about 20 other states; no payment card, bank account or health data fields; the auto-accept setting for extracted fields is on for 31 of 45 customers

title: Data dictionary, upload pipeline and AI extraction design
source_system: Repository (SYS-02): data dictionary, extraction field list, prompt template, release notes
what_it_shows: W-9 images and text are stored as uploaded; the extraction copies the full TIN into a database field shown to every customer user; the extraction worker sends the full document image and text, including TINs, to the model provider API, with document text placed in the prompt; extracted fields are labeled AI-filled with a confidence score; if the provider is unavailable, documents go to a manual review queue; the upload pipeline has no malware scanning step; release notes date the extraction release to all customers on 2026-04-20; no accuracy test results are in the repository

title: Error tracking and log management settings
source_system: Error tracking and log management console (SYS-05)
what_it_shows: Events and request logs kept 14 days; the vendor's data scrubbing option is available and off; extraction worker error events include the request payload; a search of stored events returns errors whose payloads contain text extracted from W-9s, including TINs

title: MSP device, encryption, antivirus and patch report, July 2026
source_system: MSP device management and antivirus consoles
what_it_shows: 7 company laptops enrolled in device management under the MSP's standard profile; full-disk encryption on 7 of 7; antivirus active on 7 of 7; monthly operating system and application patching; screen lock after 10 minutes idle; staff have no local administrator rights; remote wipe available, with wipe records for laptops reissued or retired; the contract developer's personal laptop is not enrolled

title: Document request response
source_system: Document request list; company shared drive
what_it_shows: The request for security policies, a risk assessment, an incident response plan, a contingency or recovery plan, a customer security contact list, incident notice templates, a retention schedule, security or secure coding training records, penetration test reports, a SOC 2 report about the company, an AI risk assessment or accuracy test results, and vendor security reviews returned none

title: Website security page and product page capture
source_system: Company website
what_it_shows: The security page says "bank-level 256-bit encryption" and "your vendors' tax IDs are encrypted and never leave our platform"; the product page says "AI reads certificates with 99% accuracy"; a link to the public status page; no published security contact or vulnerability disclosure route

title: Security questionnaire answer document and CRM records
source_system: CRM (SYS-07); company shared drive
what_it_shows: 14 customer and prospect security questionnaires answered in the 12 months to July 2026, all from a 2024 answer document; answers include "SOC 2 compliant" and "annual penetration test performed"; no approval step is recorded; 2 prospects list a SOC 2 report as a condition of signing, and one anchor customer's renewal on 2027-06-30 requires one

title: Customer MSA, DPA and security exhibit
source_system: Operations and Finance Manager's contracts folder
what_it_shows: Templates written by outside counsel in 2024 and used for all 45 customers: notice of a security incident affecting customer data without undue delay and within 72 hours of confirmation; a published sub-processor list with 30 days' notice of new sub-processors; deletion of customer data within 60 days after termination; customer data used only to provide the service, on customers' instructions; security exhibit promising encryption in transit and at rest, MFA for personnel access, annual third-party penetration testing, and daily backups retained 30 days; 99.5% monthly uptime target, with service credits in the 2 anchor customers' agreements

title: Published sub-processor list and vendor contract file
source_system: Company website; Operations and Finance Manager's contracts folder
what_it_shows: The published list names 4 sub-processors: the cloud provider, the email delivery service, the error tracking and log management service, and the support desk SaaS; signed DPAs on file with these 4; no DPA or listing for the AI model provider and no customer notice of a new sub-processor in the file; contractor agreement with a confidentiality clause and no security terms; no record of vendor security reviews

title: MSP service contract
source_system: Operations and Finance Manager's contracts folder

title: AI extraction accuracy, bias and prompt injection test, 2026-09-02
source_system: Test run by the Customer Success Manager and the Software Engineer on copies inside the production account
what_it_shows: 400 labeled documents from 12 customers (250 certificates, 100 W-9s, 50 licenses): 93.5% field-level accuracy; 7 of 250 certificates with a critical error, 3 of which would have marked an expired policy as current; 2 of 100 W-9s with the TIN type wrong; critical errors on 5 of 36 certificates received as phone photos or handwritten forms (13.9%) and on 2 of 214 clean digital PDFs (0.9%); 2 of 15 prompt injection documents changed an extracted field, and none reached another tenant's data

title: Control assessment: account management test
source_system: User lists for the cloud account, repository, admin console, support desk and suite compared with the staff and contractor roster (dated 2026-08-01); March 2026 departure email; suite sign-in log from the MSP; CTO, Operations and Finance Manager and MSP interviews
what_it_shows: Account types, approvals, role criteria and account procedures are not documented and no account review has been done; accounts are created on a chat message; the departure email of March 2026 reached the CTO and the MSP; the former Customer Success Manager's admin console and support desk accounts were active 5 months after departure, and the Account Executive kept admin console access after moving from support to sales in 2025; all 3 accounts were disabled on 2026-08-26; the support desk sign-in history shows no use after the departure, and the admin console records no sign-ins; the shared root password has not changed since 2024

title: Control assessment: least privilege test
source_system: Cloud permission export; administrator-only test action with the contract developer's account; MSP endpoint policy
what_it_shows: The CTO, both engineers, the contract developer and the CI key hold the full administrator policy; the contract developer's account completed an administrator-only tagging change in the test

title: Control assessment: privileged MFA test
source_system: MFA settings for the suite, cloud console and repository; admin console sign-in test; root account settings
what_it_shows: MFA enforced on the suite (including the MSP's 2 administrator accounts), the per-person cloud console accounts and the repository; the admin console accepted a password alone in the test; the root account's MFA device is the CTO's personal phone

title: Control assessment: authenticator management review
source_system: Access key report; CI secret list; container definitions; password manager vault entry list; MSP tickets; file listing of the contractor's personal laptop (with consent)
what_it_shows: The MSP issues suite accounts after the Operations and Finance Manager confirms the person; suite and cloud accounts start with a temporary password that must be changed; no default credentials on cloud resources, and the database administrator password was changed at creation; the CI key (March 2024) and third-party API keys have not been rotated and no rotation period is defined; the CI key is in the contractor's local environment file; application secrets are container environment variables; the root password is in a vault entry open to all engineers and the contractor and was not changed after the former Customer Success Manager and a 2025 contractor left; admin console passwords have no length rule; staff use the password manager by habit with no rule requiring it; no procedure for lost or compromised authenticators

title: Control assessment: event logging review
source_system: Cloud, bucket and database logging settings; admin console logging; CTO interview
what_it_shows: Only the provider's default management events are logged, kept 90 days; object read logging on the document bucket and database audit logging are off; logged event types have never been identified, coordinated or reviewed; the admin console records no sign-ins or view-as-customer sessions

title: Control assessment: log review interviews
source_system: CTO and Senior Software Engineer interviews; log management console
what_it_shows: Logs are read only when an engineer debugs an error; no review for unusual activity, no reporting of review results, and no process to adjust review when risk changes

title: Control assessment: backup review and restore test
source_system: Database backup settings; bucket settings; deletion and attempted restore of a test file in a copy of the bucket configuration; document storage in the suite
what_it_shows: Point-in-time recovery 7 days and daily snapshots kept 7 days, encrypted with provider-managed keys, in the production account; bucket versioning off, and a deleted test file could not be restored; about 40% of production resources built by hand with no configuration backup; snapshots are not write-once and can be deleted by any administrator or the CI key; policies, the SSP and runbooks are kept in the suite with version history

title: Control assessment: contingency test interview
source_system: CTO and Senior Software Engineer interviews; document request
what_it_shows: No contingency plan, no defined tests of effectiveness or readiness, and no restore has ever been tried

title: Control assessment: incident reporting interviews
source_system: Draft POL-03; interviews with 5 of 7 staff and the contract developer
what_it_shows: No reporting rule or time limit was in use; 3 of 5 staff interviewed did not know whom to tell of a suspected incident; no defined recipients for incident information and no customer security contact list; POL-03 was a draft

title: Control assessment: external service provider review
source_system: DPA sub-processor list; vendor contracts; model provider API terms; MSP contract; contractor agreement
what_it_shows: DPAs define the roles of the 4 listed sub-processors and the MSP contract defines the MSP's duties; no security requirements set for the AI model provider, the MSP or the contract developer; the model provider processes customer data without being on the sub-processor list and may keep inputs 30 days; no oversight process, no controls specified for providers, and no ongoing monitoring; no provider SOC 2 report had been reviewed

title: Control assessment: live data outside production
source_system: Engineer and contractor interviews; file listing of the contractor's personal laptop on a video call, with consent; MSP device reports for company laptops
what_it_shows: Copying production extracts to laptops has never been approved, documented or tracked; the contractor's laptop held 3 extracts with vendor tax IDs, the newest from 2026-07-14, and a copy of the CI key; the contractor could not show encryption status, and the laptop has no company antivirus or patch evidence

title: Control assessment: protection of data at rest
source_system: Encryption settings for the database, snapshots and bucket; MSP encryption report; customer user view of W-9 fields in a test tenant
what_it_shows: Storage encryption is on for the database, snapshots, bucket and company laptops; a customer user in a test tenant saw full Social Security numbers on W-9 fields; database extracts sat on the unmanaged personal laptop

title: Control assessment: vulnerability monitoring review
source_system: Dependency alert list; repository settings; CTO interview
what_it_shows: The repository host monitors dependencies, raises alerts for new advisories with CVE identifiers and CVSS scores, and updates its advisory database continuously; 14 High alerts older than 30 days had not been opened; container images and public endpoints are not scanned; no remediation time limits, configuration checklists or recipients for vulnerability information

title: Control assessment: external personnel security review
source_system: Contractor agreement; MSP contract; MSP technician list (received 2026-08-21); CTO, Operations and Finance Manager, contractor and MSP interviews
what_it_shows: Neither the contractor agreement nor the MSP contract sets personnel security requirements or requires compliance with company security policies; the MSP is not required to report changes of technicians with administrator access; provider compliance is not monitored, and the contractor's device had not been checked before this assessment
